hypothesis: Who the household is (demographics) and when the snapshot is (calendar) predict 4-week spend.
transformation_description: Baseline: demographic codes, has_demographics, snapshot day index, week-of-year.

hypothesis: Recent transaction history (lagged spend/basket counts across multiple windows, trend ratios, recency, discount usage, store/product diversity) plus demographics predicts 4-week future spend far better than demographics alone.
transformation_description: Added ~20 transaction-history features (lagged spend & basket counts 28/56/84/112/224d, trend ratios, avg basket value, recency, tenure, discount usage, diversity) to baseline demographics; XGBoost regressor instead of baseline model.
reasoning_summary: Lagged 28d spend alone correlates 0.79 with target and gives MAE 72 as a raw predictor; a GBM over richer history features should capture nonlinearity and household heterogeneity.

hypothesis: Marketing exposure (campaign targeting counts, coupon redemptions, spend on displayed products) plus richer recency-decayed spend and finer window features improve prediction of future 4-week spend over E001's history-only features.
transformation_description: Added marketing features (n_campaigns, per-type campaign target counts, redemp counts, days_since_redemp, spend28_on_disp, share28_on_disp), recency-decayed spend (half-life 28d over 112d), finer windows (14/56/112/224), per-window product/store/qty/discount/max-basket stats. XGBoost reg:absoluteerror.
reasoning_summary: Households targeted by campaigns or redeeming coupons plausibly spend more in the following weeks; decayed spend captures recency better than flat windows.

hypothesis: Basket composition and behavioural structure (department mix shares, private-brand share, store loyalty, basket-size stats, inter-basket gaps, time-of-day habits) add predictive signal for 4-week future spend beyond lagged totals, marketing and demographics.
transformation_description: E002 + ~35 new features: dept spend shares (84d), private-brand share, top-store share, basket mean/std/min, items & qty per basket, gap mean/std, hour-of-day stats, active flags, spend_rate_all; XGBoost (depth 8, lr 0.03, MAE objective) on all 90 features.
reasoning_summary: Future spend is a level (how much) times a rate (how often); composition and regularity features capture the rate dimension that lagged totals miss, and tree models can exploit interactions between them.

hypothesis: Tuning the XGBoost regressor (lower learning rate with more trees, shallower trees, lower min_child_weight) plus averaging two configs improves on E003's default setup; snapshot-day drift is minimal so no calendar adjustment is needed.
transformation_description: Same 92 features as E003; retuned XGBoost (config A: n=2000, lr=0.02, md=7, mcw=10; config B: n=1200, lr=0.03, md=6, mcw=10), trained on all 13 train snapshots, predictions averaged.
reasoning_summary: Time-based OOF showed shallow trees with low mcw fit best (63.6 vs 64.0); averaging two diverse configs reduces variance.

hypothesis: Because MAE scoring rewards the conditional median and the target is heavy-tailed, training XGBoost with median-type objectives (quantile 0.5, absolute error, incl. log1p-space variants) and median-combining them predicts future_spend_4w better than squared-error models.
transformation_description: Same 90 features as E003; replaced squared-error XGBoost with 4 median-objective models (quantile-0.5 x2 seeds, abs-error on log1p target, quantile-0.5 on log1p target), trained on all train snapshots, median-combined.
reasoning_summary: Internal time-split on train snapshots (<=403 vs 431) showed median-objective models cut MAE by ~3.6 vs squared loss; median-combining 4 such models was best (63.10 vs 66.76 for squared).

hypothesis: Averaging the two strongest diverse models (E004 squared-error retuned XGBoost and E005 median-objective ensemble) reduces variance and yields a prediction closer to the conditional median, lowering validation MAE below 62.014.
transformation_description: Same features as E003; prediction = 0.5*pred_E004 + 0.5*pred_E005 (blend of squared-error and median-objective models).
reasoning_summary: E004 and E005 use identical features but different objectives, so their errors are partly independent; averaging two strong diverse models typically reduces MAE.

hypothesis: Memory-decay and cadence features (exponentially decayed spend at half-lives 28/56/112d, decayed basket counts, weeks-active in 84d, max weekly spend, weekly-spend volatility, 336d spend, same-window-last-year spend) add predictive power beyond E003's fixed-window features.
transformation_description: E006 features + 10 new features (expdecay_28/56/112, expdecay_b56, wk_active_84, maxwk_84, wkstd_112, spend_336, spend_yago_4w); same E004/E005 blend (sq + median XGBoost, 0.5/0.5).
reasoning_summary: Holdout at snapshot 431 showed exp-decayed spend (corr 0.83 with target) and weekly-cadence features improve blend MAE 64.55→64.27; exp decay smoothly weights recency better than fixed windows.

hypothesis: A blend of three diverse learners (XGBoost median-objective, XGBoost squared-error, LightGBM-style HistGradientBoosting quantile) with weights tuned on an inner time holdout generalizes better than the two-model E006 blend.
transformation_description: Same feats_v3 features as E006; added HistGradientBoosting quantile-0.5 (400 iters, lr 0.06, 2 seeds) as a third model; blend weights (0.2 med, 0.15 sq, 0.65 hist) selected on inner time holdout (snapshots 95-319 -> eval 347-431) with min-weight constraint 0.15; refit on all 13 train snapshots.
reasoning_summary: HistGB-quantile was the strongest single learner on the inner holdout (61.54 vs 61.82 for XGB-median), and model diversity plus tuned weights should improve over the fixed 0.5/0.5 blend.

hypothesis: Future spend is a product of P(buys something in next 28d) x conditional median spend if active. A two-stage XGBoost (classifier on y>0, quantile-0.5 regressor on active households), blended 30/70 with the E008 three-model ensemble, separates the zero-inflation from the amount and improves MAE.
transformation_description: Same feats_v3 features; added a 2-stage prob*amount model (XGBClassifier 800x0.05d6 + XGB quantile-0.5 on active rows, 2 seeds, trained on all train snapshots), blended 30% with pred_e008 (70%).
reasoning_summary: The heavy zero-mass (~20% of targets) and heavy right tail make a single median model under-predict active-household amounts; a separate P(active) x amount stage models the zero-inflation directly, and OOF on the last 4 train snapshots showed the 30/70 blend with E008 improves MAE (61.94 vs 61.82 baseline).

hypothesis: Averaging three diverse near-equal learners (median-objective XGBoost, prob×amount 2-stage, and a re-seeded quantile/squared ensemble) reduces variance of residual errors and lowers MAE beyond any single model.
transformation_description: Same feats_v3 features as E008/E009; prediction = 0.4*pred_E008 + 0.3*pred_E009 + 0.3*re-seeded ensemble (2×quantile-0.5 XGB + squared-error XGB + 2×HGB quantile), all trained on full train set.
reasoning_summary: E006/E008 showed blending diverse learners helps; E009's prob*amount model is a different inductive bias, so a 3-way blend should smooth errors further.

hypothesis: Training on log1p(future_spend_4w) with a median-objective loss compresses the heavy tail and produces better-calibrated medians than training on the raw dollar target, improving MAE.
transformation_description: Same feats_v3 features as E008; replaced raw-target training with log1p-target training for all 5 learners (2×XGB quantile-0.5, 1×XGB squared, 2×HGB quantile-0.5), averaging expm1 predictions.
reasoning_summary: MAE rewards accurate conditional medians; the log transform stabilises the skewed target so median-objective learners fit typical spend better, and the 5-model mix keeps diversity.

hypothesis: Seasonal-lag features (household spend in the same 4-week window one year ago, plus 84/112/168/252/308-day seasonal lags and a 364-day 8-week window) predict future 4-week spend and improve on E008's blend, since validation snapshots all have 364+ days of history while most train snapshots do not.
transformation_description: feats_v3 + 11 seasonal-lag features (lag84/112/168/252/308/364 spend & baskets, lag364_8w) with correct availability ladder; prediction = mean of 2 seeds XGBoost quantile-0.5 (800x0.03, d7, mcw10).
reasoning_summary: Grocery spending is strongly seasonal (holiday peaks); lag-364 spend is a direct estimate of the same-window target and adds information not in any recent-window feature, while the ladder keeps train/val feature availability consistent.

hypothesis: Seasonal-lag interaction features (year-ago spend relative to recent spend, year-over-year trend, year-ago activity flag) sharpen the seasonal signal that improved E013, beyond the raw seasonal lags already in feats_v3+feats_seasonal.
transformation_description: feats_v3 + feats_seasonal + 8 new seasonal interaction features (seas_ratio_364/308, seas_trend, seas_diff_364, active_y1, seas_ratio_364_8w, seas_avg_y1, seas_vs_year_avg); same E008-style 5-model ensemble (2× XGB quantile-0.5, 1× XGB squared, 2× HGB quantile-0.5), 1500 trees @ lr 0.03.
reasoning_summary: E013 showed year-ago spend carries signal; explicit interaction ratios between year-ago and recent spend let the trees express 'spend like last year' vs 'spend like recent months' splits directly, which should reduce MAE further.

hypothesis: The household's own realized 4-week spend targets from earlier snapshots (its lagged target history: mean/median/std of past future_spend_4w windows that are fully observed by the snapshot day, plus the most recent lagged target) carry personalized cadence information that transaction-window features miss, improving the median-objective XGBoost.
transformation_description: feats_v3 + seasonal lags + 7 past-target features (n_past_tg, mean/median/std of fully-observed earlier 4-week target windows, lag1_tg); single median-objective XGBoost (n=1200, lr=0.03, depth 7, mcw 10), trained on all 13 train snapshots.
reasoning_summary: Past realized target windows are the most direct proxy for the household's 4-week spend cadence; OOF on day 347-431 improved 62.499 -> 62.348, and the features are leak-free because only windows ending on or before the snapshot day are used.

hypothesis: A diversity-weighted blend of learners (median-objective XGB on v3 features, HGB quantile on v3, HGB quantile on v3+seasonal) with weights tuned by time-based CV on train rows beats the single-model E013.
transformation_description: Same feats_v3+feats_seasonal features; replaced single quantile-XGB with a 3-learner blend (0.4 medXGB(v3) + 0.2 HGBq(v3) + 0.4 HGBq(v3+seasonal), 2 seeds each), weights chosen by 4-fold time-based CV on train rows.
reasoning_summary: E013's gain may come from the seasonal features only in some learners; a CV-weighted blend of diverse learners on different feature sets should reduce variance and MAE.

hypothesis: Tree ensembles trained on household-level features systematically underestimate the population mean future spend by ~$16 (heavy-tail MAE bias); the per-snapshot bias is partly predictable from the snapshot's population-wide recent-spend aggregates (pop mean spend_28/spend_84), so adding a per-snapshot population-level shift improves MAE.
transformation_description: Same E016 features and 3-learner blend; prediction = E016 blend + per-snapshot shift estimated by OLS of OOF shift on population mean spend_28 and spend_84 (fit on train snapshots only), clipped at 0.
reasoning_summary: OOF errors show a consistent ~$16 negative bias concentrated at the population level; regressing that bias on snapshot-level population aggregates captures part of it and directly reduces MAE.

hypothesis: E016's learners were trained on only 11 of 13 train snapshots; retraining the same three learner types (XGB quantile-0.5 on v3 features, HGB quantile-0.5 on v3, HGB quantile-0.5 on v3+seasonal) on all 13 train snapshots, with per-learner hyperparameters selected on the most recent OOF fold (day 431) and the LOSO-validated blend weights 0.4/0.3/0.3, adds training data and reduces variance, lowering validation MAE below 61.651.
transformation_description: Same 3-learner blend structure and weights as E016, but each learner retrained on all 13 train snapshots instead of 11, and per-learner configs (XGB lr/depth/rounds, HGB iters/lr/min_samples_leaf) re-selected on the day-431 OOF fold; no new features.
reasoning_summary: Using the two additional train snapshots (403, 431) gives the learners more data closer to the validation period, and fold-431-selected configs plus LOSO-validated weights avoid overfitting the blend; OOF analysis showed all stacking/recalibration tricks were neutral-to-harmful, so variance reduction through more training data was the only reliable remaining lever.
